fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 趙王倫、孫秀將討賈后，告右衛佽飛督閭和，和從之，期以癸巳丙夜一籌，以鼓聲為應。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Lun and Xiu prepared to move against the empress, won over Lü He, Colonel of the Right Guards Attendants, and set guisi night, second watch of the bing hour, drums as signal.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: The Prince of Zhao Lun and Sun Xiu were about to attack Empress Jia; they told the Colonel of the Right Guards Attendants Lü He, who joined them, fixing the night of guisi on the second watch of the bing hour, with drumbeats as signal.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 癸巳，秀使司馬雅告張華曰：「趙王欲與公共匡社稷，為天下除害，使雅以告。」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join you to save the realm and remove this evil."
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join with you to steady the altars, remove harm for the realm—Ya reports this."

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 華拒之。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Hua refused.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Hua refused.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 雅怒曰：「刃將加頸，猶為是言邪！」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Ya snapped: "The blade is at your neck and you still talk like that!"
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Ya angrily said: "The blade is at the neck—yet you speak thus!"

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 不顧而出。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: He strode out without a backward glance.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: He left without looking back.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 及期，倫矯詔敕三部司馬曰：「中宮與賈謐等殺吾太子，今使車騎入廢中宮，汝等皆當從命，事畢，賜爵關中侯，不從者誅三族。」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: At the hour Lun forged an edict to the three departments: "The empress and Jia Mi killed the heir apparent. The Cavalry General enters to depose her. Obey and receive marquisates; disobey and face extermination."
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: When the hour came Lun forged an edict instructing the three departments' majors: "The central palace and Jia Mi and others killed our Heir Apparent; the Cavalry General will enter and depose the central palace—you must all obey. When done, enfeoffment as marquis within the passes; disobedience exterminates three clans."

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 眾皆從之。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: All obeyed.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: All obeyed.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 又矯詔開門，夜入，陳兵道南，遣翊軍校尉齊王冏將百人排冏而入，華林令駱休為內應，迎帝幸東堂，以詔召賈謐於殿前，將誅之。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: He forged orders to open the gates, entered at night, lined troops along the southern route, sent Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, with a hundred men to force entry, Luo Xiu of Hualin as inside agent, escorted the emperor to the Eastern Hall, and summoned Jia Mi to execution.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: He also forged an edict to open the gates, entered by night, arrayed troops along the southern way, sent the Colonel of the Supports the Prince of Qi Sima Jiong with a hundred men to force the gates and enter, the Commandant of the Hualin Park Luo Xiu as inside agent, brought the emperor to the Eastern Hall, and by edict summoned Jia Mi before the hall to be executed.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 謐走入西鐘下，呼曰：「阿后救我！」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Mi fled to the western bell-frame crying: "Mother, save me!"
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Mi ran beneath the western bell-frame crying: "Mother, save me!"

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 就斬之。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: He was beheaded at once.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: He was beheaded on the spot.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 賈后見齊王冏，驚曰：「卿何為來？」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Seeing Sima Jiong the empress cried: "Why are you here?"
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: When Empress Jia saw Sima Jiong she exclaimed: "Why have you come?"

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 冏曰：「有詔收后。」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Jiong said: "An edict commands your arrest."
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Jiong said: "There is an edict to take the empress."

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 后曰：「詔當從我出，何詔也！」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: She said: "Edicts should come from me—what edict is this!"
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: The empress said: "Edicts should come from me—what edict is this!"

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 后至上閤，遙呼帝曰：「陛下有婦，使人廢之，亦行自廢矣。」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: She climbed to the upper pavilion and called to the emperor: "You have a wife; when others depose her, you will be deposed yourself."
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: She went up to the upper pavilion and called to the emperor from afar: "Your Majesty has a consort; when others deposed her, you too will be deposed."

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 是時，梁王肜亦預其謀，后問冏曰：「起事者誰？」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: The Prince of Liang Sima Rong was also in the plot; she asked Jiong: "Who raised this?"
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: At that time the Prince of Liang Sima Rong also took part in the plot; the empress asked Jiong: "Who raised the affair?"

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 冏曰：「梁、趙。」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Jiong said: "Liang and Zhao."
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Jiong said: "Liang and Zhao."

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 后曰：「系狗當繫頸，反系其尾，何得不然！」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: She said: "Tie a dog by the neck, not the tail—was this not inevitable!"
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: The empress said: "When tying a dog one should tie the neck—instead they tied the tail; how could it not turn out thus!"

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 遂廢后為庶人，幽之於建始殿，收趙粲、賈午等付暴室考竟。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: She was deposed as a commoner and confined in the Jianshi Hall; Zhao Can, Jia Wu, and others were sent to the Severe Chamber for interrogation unto death.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: She was thereupon deposed as commoner and confined in the Jianshi Hall; Zhao Can, Jia Wu, and others were taken to the Severe Chamber for interrogation to the death.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 詔尚書收捕賈氏親黨，召中書監、侍中、黃門侍郎、八座皆夜入殿。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: An edict ordered arrest of the Jia clan; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and Eight Seats were summoned at night.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: An edict ordered the Masters of Writing to arrest the Jia kin; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and the Eight Seats were all summoned into the hall at night.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 尚書始疑詔有詐，郎師景露版奏請手詔，倫等斬之以徇。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: The Masters of Writing doubted the edict; Gentleman Shi Jing asked for the emperor's own hand; Lun beheaded him as warning.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: The Masters of Writing at first doubted the edict was false; Gentleman Shi Jing displayed the tablet and asked for a handwritten edict; Lun and the rest beheaded him as a warning.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 中護軍淮南王允，性沉毅，宿衛將士皆畏服之。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Yun, Prince of Huainan, Central Protector of the Army, was deep and resolute by nature, and the palace guards all feared him.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: The Central Protector of the Army, the Prince of Huainan Yun, was by nature deep and resolute; the garrison soldiers all feared and submitted to him.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 允知相國倫及孫秀有異志，陰養死士，謀討之；
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Knowing Lun and Xiu meant to rebel, he secretly gathered men willing to die and plotted against them;
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Yun knew Chancellor Lun and Sun Xiu harbored rebellious intent and secretly nurtured men willing to die, plotting to attack them;

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 倫、秀深憚之。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Lun and Xiu feared him deeply.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Lun and Xiu deeply dreaded him.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 秋，八月，轉允為太尉，外示優崇，實奪其兵權。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: In autumn, the eighth month, he was transferred to Grand Commandant, an outward honor that in fact stripped him of military command.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Yun was transferred to Grand Commandant—outwardly a mark of honor, in reality his military power was taken away.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 允稱疾不拜。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: He pleaded illness and refused the appointment.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Yun pleaded illness and would not accept the appointment.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 秀遣御史劉機逼允，收其官屬以下，劾以拒詔，大逆不敬。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Xiu sent Censor Liu Ji to coerce him, arrested his staff, and charged him with resisting an edict and great impiety.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Xiu sent the Censor Liu Ji to press Yun, seized his officials and subordinates, and impeached him for resisting an edict, great irreverence and impiety.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 允視詔，乃秀手書也，大怒，收御史，將斬之，御史走免，斬其令史二人。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Yun saw the edict was in Xiu's own hand, flew into a rage, seized the censor and nearly executed him; the censor fled, and two clerks were beheaded.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Yun looked at the edict—it was in Xiu's own hand—and grew greatly angry, seized the censor, and was about to behead him; the censor fled and escaped, and two clerks were beheaded.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 厲色謂左右曰：「趙王欲破我家！」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: He said grimly to his attendants: "The Prince of Zhao means to destroy my house!"
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: With stern countenance he said to those at his side: "The Prince of Zhao means to destroy my house!"

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 遂帥國兵及帳下七百人直出，大呼曰：「趙王反，我將討之，從我者左袒。」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: He led his state troops and seven hundred household guards straight out, shouting: "The Prince of Zhao has rebelled! I shall punish him. Follow me and bare your left shoulder."
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: He thereupon led his state troops and seven hundred men of his personal guard straight out, shouting loudly: "The Prince of Zhao has rebelled—I shall punish him; those who follow me, bare your left shoulder."

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 於是歸之者甚眾。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Many rallied to him.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: At this very many came over to him.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 允將赴宮，尚書左丞王輿閉掖門，允不得入，遂圍相府。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Yun marched on the palace, but Wang Yu, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, shut the side gate and blocked him; he then besieged the chancellor's residence.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Yun was about to go to the palace; the Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yu closed the side gate, and Yun could not enter; he thereupon besieged the chancellor's mansion.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 允所將兵皆精銳，倫與戰，屢敗，死者千餘人。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Yun's troops were elite. Lun fought him repeatedly and lost, with more than a thousand dead.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: The troops Yun led were all elite; Lun fought him and was repeatedly defeated, more than a thousand dead.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 太子左率陳徽勒東宮兵，鼓噪於內以應允。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Chen Hui, Colonel of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent, stirred Eastern Palace troops to cheer within in support of Yun.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Chen Hui, Colonel of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent, roused Eastern Palace troops and clamored within in support of Yun.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 允結陳於承華門前，弓弩齊發，射倫，飛矢雨下。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Yun formed battle lines before the Chenghua Gate. Bows and crossbows volleyed at Lun until arrows fell like rain.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Yun drew up his array before the Chenghua Gate; bows and crossbows fired together, shooting at Lun—arrows fell like rain.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 主書司馬眭秘以身蔽倫，箭中其背而死。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Chief Clerk Sima Sui shielded Lun with his body and was killed by an arrow in the back.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: The Chief Clerk Sima Sui shielded Lun with his body; an arrow struck his back and he died.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 倫官屬皆隱樹而立，每樹輒中數百箭，自辰至未，中書令陳淮，徽之兄也，欲應允，言於帝曰：「宜遣白虎幡以解鬥。」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Lun's staff hid behind trees, each tree studded with hundreds of arrows. From chen to wei, Chen Huai, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Hui's elder brother, wished to aid Yun and told the emperor: "Send the white tiger banner to stop the fighting."
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Lun's staff all hid behind trees to stand; each tree received hundreds of arrows. From the hour chen to wei, the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Chen Huai—Hui's elder brother—wished to support Yun and said to the emperor: "The white tiger banner should be sent to halt the fighting."

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 乃使司馬督護伏胤將騎四百持幡從宮中出。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: The Major of the Protectorate Fu Yin was sent with four hundred horsemen bearing the banner from the palace.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: He then had the Major Fu Yin of the Protectorate lead four hundred horsemen bearing the banner out from within the palace.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 侍中汝陰王虔在門下省，陰與胤誓曰：「富貴當與卿共之。」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: The Attendant, Prince of Runan Qian, was in the Gate Department and secretly swore to Yin: "We shall share wealth and honor."
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: The Attendant, the Prince of Runan Qian, was in the Gate Department; he secretly swore with Yin: "Wealth and honor shall be shared with you."

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 胤乃懷空板出，詐言有詔助淮南王。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Yin carried out a blank tablet and falsely claimed an edict to aid the Prince of Huainan.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Yin then carried a blank tablet out and falsely said there was an edict to aid the Prince of Huainan.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 允不之覺，開陣內之，下車受詔；
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Yun did not detect the fraud and opened his ranks. Yin dismounted to receive the edict;
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Yun did not perceive the deception and opened his ranks to admit him; Yin dismounted to receive the edict;

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 胤因殺之，並殺允子秦王郁、漢王迪，坐允夷滅者數千人。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Yin then killed him, along with Yun's sons Yu, Prince of Qin, and Di, Prince of Han. Several thousand connected with Yun were exterminated.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Yin thereupon killed him, and also killed Yun's sons, the Prince of Qin Yu and the Prince of Han Di; those implicated with Yun and exterminated numbered several thousand.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 曲赦洛陽。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: A partial amnesty was granted to Luoyang.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: A partial amnesty was granted to Luoyang.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 初，孫秀嘗為小吏，事黃門郎潘岳，岳屢撻之。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Earlier Xiu had served as a petty clerk under Pan Yue, Yellow Gate Gentleman, whom he had often flogged.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Earlier Sun Xiu had once been a petty clerk serving the Yellow Gate Gentleman Pan Yue; Yue often flogged him.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 衛尉石崇之甥歐陽建素與相國倫有隙，崇有愛妾曰綠珠，孫秀便求之，崇不與。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Ouyang Jian, nephew of Commandant of the Guards Shi Chong, was estranged from Lun. Chong had a beloved concubine, Green Pearl, whom Xiu demanded and Chong refused.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Ouyang Jian, nephew of the Commandant of the Guards Shi Chong, had long been at odds with Chancellor Lun; Chong had a beloved concubine named Green Pearl whom Sun Xiu asked for, but Chong would not give her.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 及淮南王允敗，秀因稱石崇、潘岳、歐陽建奉允為亂，收之。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: When Yun fell, Xiu accused Chong, Yue, and Jian of supporting his rebellion and arrested them.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: When the Prince of Huainan Yun was defeated, Xiu thereupon claimed that Shi Chong, Pan Yue, and Ouyang Jian supported Yun in rebellion and arrested them.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 崇歎曰：「奴輩利吾財爾！」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Chong sighed: "These slaves want my wealth!"
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Chong sighed: "These slaves covet my wealth!"

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 收者曰：「知財為禍，何不早散之？」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: The arresters said: "If wealth brings disaster, why not have given it away?"
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: The arresters said: "Knowing wealth brings disaster, why not have dispersed it early?"

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 崇不能答。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Chong had no answer.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Chong could not answer.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 初，潘岳母常誚責岳曰：「汝當知足，而乾沒不已乎！」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Earlier Yue's mother had often scolded him: "Know when you have enough—why keep grasping for more?"
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Earlier Pan Yue's mother often reproached Yue, saying: "You ought to know sufficiency—why seize and scrape without end!"

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 及敗，岳謝母曰：「負阿母。」
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: When ruin came Yue told his mother: "I have failed you, Mother."
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: When disaster came Yue apologized to his mother: "I have failed you, Mother."

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 遂與崇，建皆族誅，籍沒崇家。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Yue, Chong, and Jian were executed to the clan, and Chong's estate was confiscated.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Thereupon Yue, Chong, and Jian were all executed to the clan, and Chong's property was confiscated.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 相國倫收淮南王母弟吳王晏，欲殺之。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Lun arrested Yan, Prince of Wu, younger brother of Yun's mother, intending to kill him.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: Chancellor Lun arrested the Prince of Wu Yan, younger brother of the Prince of Huainan's mother, intending to kill him.

fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.zh: 光祿大夫傅祗爭之於朝堂，眾皆諫止倫，倫乃貶晏為賓徒縣王。
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.en: Household Grandee Fu Zhi argued for him in court; all remonstrated, and Lun degraded Yan to Prince of Bintu.
fullChineseAndPairedEnglishFrames.literal: The Household Grandee Fu Zhi contended for him in the court hall; all remonstrated and stopped Lun, and Lun thereupon degraded Yan to Prince of Bintu county.

value.event: Sima Yun refused the Grand Commandant post, rose against Sima Lun and besieged the chancellor's residence

value.event: Sima Lun fought off Sima Yun's attack and then received the Nine Bestowals

definitions: King of Wu; Prince of Wu

allZhongshujian.en: An edict ordered arrest of the Jia clan; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and Eight Seats were summoned at night.
allZhongshujian.literal: An edict ordered the Masters of Writing to arrest the Jia kin; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and the Eight Seats were all summoned into the hall at night.

allMudi.en: Lun arrested Yan, Prince of Wu, younger brother of Yun's mother, intending to kill him.
allMudi.literal: Chancellor Lun arrested the Prince of Wu Yan, younger brother of the Prince of Huainan's mother, intending to kill him.

oldActualAppliedRepairs: Xin made Xiu General Who Subdues Bandits and Marquis of Yangquan Pavilion, entrusted him as close confidant, and had him gather braves of the six commanderies to more than ten thousand to cut the northern road.

Xin made Li Xiang General Who Subdues Bandits and Marquis of Yangquan Pavilion, entrusted him as close confidant, and had him gather braves of the six commanderies to more than ten thousand to cut the northern road.

In the continuous Zhao Xin frame, s0385 explicitly names 李庠 joining 廞, then s0386 廞以庠 appoints that same Li Xiang. 孫秀 belongs to the separate s0354 empress episode. Accept only the proposed Xiu to Li Xiang replacement in this field; no date or other wording change is approved.
Xin made Xiu General Who Subdues Bandits and Marquis of Yangquan, trusted him deeply, and had him gather more than ten thousand braves of six commanderies to block the northern road.
